html:
The Rarámuri, also called Tarahumara, are an Indigenous people of the Sierra Madre Occidental in Chihuahua, northern Mexico. They speak a Uto-Aztecan language. The map shape also takes in their close kin the Guarijío.

They farm maize and beans in small plots, keep goats, and live spread out across canyons and pine uplands, moving between summer and winter homes. They are famous for long-distance running, including foot races in which teams kick a wooden ball for many miles.

Jesuit missionaries from New Spain reached them in the early 1600s. Several revolts in the middle of that century failed, and many Rarámuri moved deeper into the mountains, around the Copper Canyon, to stay free of missions and silver mines. Their neighbours included the Ópata and the Tepehuán. With some 85,000 people, they are one of the larger Indigenous peoples of Mexico.
